scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The work addresses an important architectural transition in multi-agent LLM systems by treating shared memory as a governed distributed-systems problem rather than solely a context retrieval task. The experimental design is rigorous, transparently reporting system anomalies, remediations, and performance trade-offs with fully committed trace artifacts.

writes). Each chain corresponds to a synthetic incident nar-
rative drawn from a pool of25operational topics (cycled,
with a per-chain nonce keeping content distinct) (e.g.,check-
out error rate spike,Kafka consumer rebalance loop). The
four steps in each chain correspond toobservation,hypothe-
sis,mitigation, andverification. Each step writes a memory
withmetadata.derived_fromencoding the parent identi-
fier. After all writes settle, the harness fetches the leaf and
walks the chain back to the root, grading three signals:
•completeness— every ancestor on the planned chain is
reachable viaGET.
•accuracy— at each step the observed writer matches
the planned writer.
•depth_fidelity— the reconstructed chain length equals
the planned depth.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are established through deterministic canary matching, HTTP error/success status verification, and graph link traversal rather than an internal or reused LLM judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The final evaluation relies on deterministic, objective black-box client probes measuring HTTP response codes, exact canary token presence, and primary-key derivation-chain integrity via the ArgusFleet harness.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The service architecture and its enforcement pipelines (e.g., semantic deduplication thresholding and RDF-triple contradiction logic) were configured and iteratively patched to satisfy governance predicates.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are precisely aligned with the empirical findings. The authors do not overclaim perfect security or universal superiority over baselines, explicitly qualifying success rates (e.g., contradiction detection succeeding 90/90 conditional on admission) and acknowledging operational trade-offs such as elevated write latency tails.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation measures the live MemClaw service across 200 trials per failure dimension, reporting exact success counts, latency percentiles, and 95% Wilson confidence intervals. It rigorously isolates confounding artifacts (such as decoupling probe-scheduling latency from server consistency latency) and highlights negative and architectural findings, including a pipeline clash between deduplication and asynchronous contradiction detection as well as a disclosed sub-tenant access gap.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are established through deterministic canary matching, HTTP error/success status verification, and graph link traversal rather than an internal or reused LLM judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The final evaluation relies on deterministic, objective black-box client probes measuring HTTP response codes, exact canary token presence, and primary-key derivation-chain integrity via the ArgusFleet harness.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The service architecture and underlying heuristics/pipelines (e.g., semantic deduplication thresholding and RDF-triple contradiction logic) were configured and iteratively patched to satisfy governance predicates.

primary.limitations: The authors provide an extensive limitations section covering the lack of comparative baselines, self-evaluation risks, single-tenant scope, and the initial lack of sub-tenant enforcement on GET-by-id.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly described, combining a formal problem specification with concrete, reproducible black-box API experiments using deterministic seeding, distinct read/write phases, and canary tokens. The harness probes both positive operational pathways and failure boundaries, documenting exact request sequences and handling API concurrency limits.
primary.quality_rationale: The work addresses an important architectural transition in multi-agent LLM systems by treating shared memory as a governed distributed-systems problem rather than solely a context retrieval task. The experimental design is rigorous, transparently reporting system anomalies, remediations, and performance trade-offs with fully committed trace artifacts.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formalizes the fleet-memory problem for multi-agent LLM systems with five primitives (agents, substrate, governance, provenance, temporal supersession) and four associated failure modes. It presents MemClaw as an implementation and ArgusFleet as an empirical evaluation harness measuring scope leakage, provenance reconstruction, propagation latency/visibility, and contradiction resolution on a running production service.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work addresses an important architectural transition in multi-agent LLM systems by treating shared memory as a governed distributed-systems problem rather than solely a context retrieval task. The experimental design is rigorous, transparently reporting system anomalies, remediations, and performance trade-offs with fully committed trace artifacts.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors provide an extensive limitations section covering the lack of comparative baselines, self-evaluation risks, single-tenant scope, and the initial lack of sub-tenant enforcement on GET-by-id.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
